items.note: Component renamed (shipped as ds-auth-shell in the tagged 0.8.0 source, its only release under that name). "Shell" is not this library's word for a layout: the app-level one was renamed ds-app-shell -> ds-app-layout in 0.7.0, and calling the auth counterpart a shell put the split vocabulary back. ACTION: rename the element and its closing tag. Behaviour, inputs and slots are unchanged - brand, logoLetter, tagline, cardElevation, cardPadding, [brand], [dsBrandName] and dsAuthSupport all keep their names. Also rename the class and the tokens (separate entries below).
The exported component class renamed alongside the ds-auth-shell -> ds-auth-layout selector. Update imports and any type references. No members changed.

Prefix rename for the six component tokens: --ds-auth-shell-min-height / -card-max-width / -gap / -bg-color / -mark-bg-color / -mark-label-color -> --ds-auth-layout-*. Values and defaults are unchanged. DS-owned tokens only (no others ship under this prefix); a consumer's own --ds-auth-shell-* variable is out of scope. EXCLUDED, do not rename: the global scale token --auth-card-w, the fallback behind -card-max-width, which carries no --ds-auth-shell- prefix and keeps its name. Confirm the new name exists in the installed package.

informational: The ds-auth-shell -> ds-auth-layout rename is vocabulary only: no input, output, slot, token value or behaviour changed, and it is the same component 0.8.0 shipped. If you never adopted ds-auth-shell (it was added in 0.8.0), there is nothing to do.

FIXED in ds-textarea: size="sm" and size="lg" rendered the md vertical padding (12px top and bottom) regardless of the size. The size blocks set the inner textarea's vertical pad, but a :host-prefixed pin at the end of the file out-ranked them once emulated encapsulation shimmed both selectors - it carries one more attribute than the size selector. There are now three pins, one per size, and the size blocks keep only the horizontal padding they own. NO ACTION: the change is visible only on a non-md textarea and the md default is unchanged. Note that retuning --ds-input-pad-y previously moved all three sizes together; if you compensated for the wrong padding with your own override on a sm or lg textarea, that override now stacks on the corrected value and can go.

ds-auth-layout now COMPRESSES its own chrome on a short viewport: block padding, the column gap, the letter-mark tile and its glyph, the wordmark and the masthead inner gap all clamp against svh. No action - behaviour only, and a viewport 800px tall or more renders exactly what it did before, so desktop is unchanged. Below that the furniture shrinks so it is not what pushes a card into scrolling (~131px instead of ~219px at a landscape phone's ~330px). Two new tokens opt out per dimension: --ds-auth-layout-pad-block and --ds-auth-layout-mark-size; setting any of those or the existing --ds-auth-layout-gap to a fixed value stops that one compressing. A card taller than the remaining space still scrolls - that is intended.

ds-icon now logs a dev-mode warning when an icon name is in neither the DS set nor your provideDsIcons() registry - previously it rendered an empty <svg> silently. No action, and nothing changes in production. Expect the warning to surface real typos the moment you upgrade: an audit of three screens in one consumer is what prompted it.

ds-app-layout gained scrollReset: "path" | "never" | "always" (default "path" = existing behaviour, so NO ACTION), and LayoutNavigationService is now exported. If you wrote your own "did the path change?" check to work around the layout resetting scroll - or to skip a view transition, or to reset a tab - replace it with inject(LayoutNavigationService).pathChanged: it is NavigationEnd, path only, de-duplicated, and it skips a navigation carrying state: { dsSamePage: true }. Note a naive split("?") is NOT equivalent, it keeps the fragment this stream strips. To stop the layout resetting scroll on a paged or filtered list, set scrollReset="never" and call LayoutScrollService.scrollToTop() where you actually want it.

Options in ds-select / ds-autocomplete / ds-multi-select panels now have a pressed state (they had hover only, which does nothing on touch). No action - visual only. If you styled :active on .option yourself to work around it, you can drop that override; if you want a different pressed fill, it reads --surface-muted (neutral rows) and --primary-subtitle (the selected row).
